name: bedrok
description: Public macroeconomic data from central banks, statistics offices and international organisations, each series fetched from its publisher into a local store. No keys needed to start.
long_description: Bedrok gives your assistant more than 700 curated series and their deep history: US rates and the Fed's releases, US labour and prices, the euro area country by country, the UK, OECD, BIS, IMF, national statistics offices, commodities, positioning and FX. Each series comes from the publisher that produces it, with its licence and the line to credit it with. Most of it works without keys; free keys add US GDP and PCE (BEA), retail and housing (Census), energy (EIA), Germany's and Japan's national statistics (Destatis, e-Stat) and the series only FRED publishes. Your data stays on your machine. Bedrok measures and contextualises; it never gives investment advice.

tools.name: list_sources
tools.description: Every publisher Bedrok is wired to, whether its key is set, and its terms

tools.name: search_series
tools.description: Find a series in the curated catalog

tools.name: list_series
tools.description: Walk the whole catalog, or count it by publisher, place and frequency

tools.name: describe_series
tools.description: Units, publisher, licence, caveats, freshness, next release and related series

tools.name: get_series
tools.description: Observations, optionally as year-on-year, 3-month annualised or rebased

tools.name: chart_series
tools.description: Series on one calendar with a chart recipe: title, units, scales, source line, footnotes

tools.name: percentile
tools.description: Where a value sits in its own history, always with the sample

tools.name: release_calendar
tools.description: When official numbers come out: a series' next release, or the week's

tools.name: query
tools.description: Read-only SQL over the local store

tools.name: refresh
tools.description: Bring stored series up to date from their publishers

data_dir.title: Bedrok folder (optional)
data_dir.description: Where Bedrok keeps its store. Leave blank for the standard folder (~/Library/Application Support/bedrok). An existing folder's .env keys are read too.

bls_api_key.title: BLS API key (optional)
bls_api_key.description: Raises the Bureau of Labor Statistics limit from 25 to 500 requests a day. Free: data.bls.gov/registrationEngine

bea_api_key.title: BEA API key (optional)
bea_api_key.description: US GDP and PCE prices. Free: apps.bea.gov/API/signup

census_api_key.title: Census API key (optional)
census_api_key.description: US retail sales, durable goods, housing, trade. Free: api.census.gov/data/key_signup.html

fred_api_key.title: FRED API key (optional)
fred_api_key.description: Series only FRED publishes (credit spreads, VIX, jobless claims), fetched live and never stored. Free: fredaccount.stlouisfed.org/apikeys

destatis_api_key.title: Destatis API token (optional)
destatis_api_key.description: Germany's national CPI and industrial production from GENESIS-Online. Free: destatis.de/EN/Service/OpenData/api-webservice.html

estat_api_key.title: e-Stat application ID (optional)
estat_api_key.description: Japan's CPI (core and core-core) and unemployment rate. Free: e-stat.go.jp/api/en
